Aug 3, 2026 (EST)

🔥 Top Stories
• Trump says Iran talks are “going on now” — claimed phase one is reopening Hormuz; later U.S. officials said no new direct talks are planned, just mediated channels.
• Oil sinks on easing Iran risk — WTI fell 5.1% to $80.34, Brent -4.7% to $83.77 as diplomacy chatter cut the war premium.
• Amazon tops $3 trillion — AMZN hit a record high and joined the $3T club, lifting megacap tech and the broader market.
• ISM manufacturing jumps to 55.6 — strongest in four years, with better orders and employment, reinforcing a resilient U.S. growth backdrop.

⛽ Oil & Energy
• Hormuz remains constrained — traffic stayed thin; Iran kept pushing its own route while ship tracking showed ongoing diversion patterns.
• SPR falls to 304.8M barrels — U.S. crude stockpile hit its lowest since 1983, underscoring tighter emergency buffers.
• Kazakhstan output drops 14% — CPC disruption hit July oil and condensate production.
• Iraq sold 42M barrels in July — stronger exports from southern ports offset weak Kirkuk-Ceyhan flows.

📊 Markets & Macro
• S&P 500 / Nasdaq rally — stocks surged as lower oil eased inflation fears; megacaps led while bonds also firmed.
• Deutsche Bank lifts S&P EPS outlook — raised 2026/27 EPS forecasts on broad Q2 beat rates and profit strength.
• U.S. bills auction solid — 3- and 6-month auctions cleared at lower yields, easing near-term funding pressure.
• Treasury raises Q3 borrowing estimate — now $739B, higher than prior forecast amid large cash needs.

🌍 Geopolitical
• Russia-Ukraine tensions persist — reports of strikes and rising casualties kept Eastern Europe risk elevated.
• Iran diplomacy remains volatile — Tehran and U.S. still trade mixed signals while regional mediators seek a path forward.
• Pakistan / Switzerland / others engage on Iran — back-channel diplomacy widened as Hormuz tensions escalated.

🪙 Crypto & DeFi
• Strategy sold 1,637 BTC — trimmed holdings to 842,138 BTC while raising cash; Saylor said he never sold personal bitcoin.
• Bitcoin rebounded above $64K — risk appetite improved alongside falling oil and a softer macro shock.
• BlackRock launched tokenized money-market fund on Ethereum — another TradFi-to-chain move.
• Bitget exits Japan — will shut remaining operations by year-end.

🏛️ Regulatory & Policy
• U.S. tightens robot import rules — FCC to restrict certain foreign advanced robots, potentially pressuring China-linked suppliers.
• White House expands AI oversight — major AI firms invited to review framework and model-testing plans.
• Apple challenges UK encryption demand — legal fight over government “back door” access escalates.
• NY AG blasts Trump tariffs — says latest tariffs are overly broad and legally problematic.

🏢 Corporate
• Palantir beats and raises — strong Q2 revenue/EPS and higher FY outlook reinforced AI/software momentum.
• Snap beats on revenue and EBITDA — DAUs topped estimates; ad recovery looks intact.
• Vertex beats revenue, guides higher — biotech held up well on solid sales and stable EPS.
• Marriott and Tyson mixed — both beat on some metrics but guided softer in spots; consumer demand remains selective.
• Meta / Google / Anthropic head to White House — AI safety testing and policy talks could shape near-term regulation.
• Visa to buy Biocatch for $2.4B — payments security M&A continues.
• JPMorgan expands housing push — now targeting $750B through 2035 to boost U.S. supply and affordability.
